text:
maria: quick thread — thinking about the 'acceptance shape' for model onboarding. I'm worried our current binary gate (pass/fail) is causing lots of churn for small, explainable diffs.

maria: proposal: support a 'fuzzy' acceptance mode for a subset of models where we do staged acceptance with observable rollback windows. not a free pass — just structured tolerance.

lee: +1 to staged. can you sketch what 'fuzzy' looks like concretely? thresholds, steps, who approves?

maria: rough sketch below — imagine a compact policy attached to a model descriptor. it runs: smoke -> shadow -> canary (1% traffic) -> ramp. scoring combines latency, token regressions, and golden-match ratio.

maria: ```json
{
  "policy": "fuzzy",
  "steps": ["smoke","shadow","canary","ramp"],
  "thresholds": {
    "latency_ms_p95": 200,
    "rtp_delta_pct": 5,
    "gold_match_pct": 90
  },
  "canary_fraction": 0.01,
  "rollback_window_mins": 60
}
```

aj: nit: gold_match_pct needs to be clearer — is that exact string match, semantic similarity, or eval score? these mean very different things.

sophia: agree with aj. recommend we treat golden-match as an eval-score distribution (KL or Spearman) and allow per-model metric names. keep generic fields but let model team map them.

lee: tradeoffs: fuzzy reduces false-negatives (blocks on non-actionable diffs) but increases risk of slow drift reaching prod. we need telemetry hooks to detect drift fast. what infra work is needed? @devon?

devon: infra needs two things: 1) per-model policy store + versioning, 2) realtime aggregator to compute these composite scores and emit alerts. can reuse probe pipeline but need tighter SLAs. estimate 2 sprints for MVP.

maria: ops question: how do we present this in Console? show an 'acceptance funnel' with pass/fail and fuzzy-state (shadow health, canary health, time to rollback). UX should make it explicit when models are in fuzzy ramp.

sophia: also think about API-side contract: should callers be able to opt-in to traffic on a fuzzy model? or do we control routing entirely server-side? my leaning: server-side only, else client fragmentation.

lee: long-term refactor: unify policy into model descriptor and move policy evaluation into a dedicated gate service. advantage: consistent enforcement across hosted/dedicated/private. downside: more infra surface.

aj: question: what about tokenizer noise and byte-level differences that trigger eval flakiness? proposal: add a lightweight normalization step in smoke to canonicalize tokenization before comparison. reduces spurious regressions.

maria: good call. add normalization stage to smoke and shadow phases. we should document allowed normalizers per model in descriptor.

devon: implementation note: we can implement normalization as a configurable middleware in the prober runner. low-effort.

lee: ops playbook: if canary health dips but within fuzzy thresholds, we hold and trigger a queued human review with auto-capture of diffs + golden examples. need 24/7 oncall integration.

maria: action items: 1) infra: prototype gate service + aggregator (devon) 2) ml: define canonical normalizers and per-model metric mapping (sophia + aj) 3) ux: acceptance funnel mockups (lee) 4) doc: update onboarding runbook to describe fuzzy semantics (maria). Can we aim for a spike + demo in 2 weeks?

devon: 👍 I'll scope and post a short plan to this channel tomorrow.

ingest-bot: canary job started for model: rwd-xl-v1 (job id: cj-179912) — shadowing traffic at 1%

sophia: thanks — I'll prepare a small golden set and a normalization matrix to avoid tokenization surprises.

maria: thanks all. if anyone has strong objections to the fuzzy concept, speak up now; otherwise we'll iterate on the plan and surface a formal RFC after the spike. :thumbsup:
